FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DOCUMENT. The materials, laboratories and measurements below are invented for software testing.

Practical notes on reference electrode calibration for alkaline electrolysis

Reference electrodes drift during long experiments, and an uncorrected drift of a few tens of millivolts can be mistaken for catalyst degradation.

We recommend calibrating mercury oxide reference electrodes against a reversible hydrogen electrode in the same electrolyte before and after every durability test. In our hands, an unattended mercury oxide electrode drifted by 22 mV over 72 hours in 1 M KOH at 25 °C.

We also recommend reporting the electrolyte temperature, because the reversible hydrogen electrode potential shifts with temperature. Durability claims that rely on a potential change smaller than the expected reference drift should be treated with caution.

These notes do not report catalyst performance data.
